***Please note that this is an award notice and not a call for competition***

This procurement was awarded following a competitive procurement exercise via the RM3764.3 - Cyber Security Services 3 DPS.

The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) is responsible for ensuring that the UK has a resilient energy sector. With the increasing use of cyber as an offensive attack methodology, and an increasing pool of adversaries prepared to employ it, action is required to support the energy sector and protect critical infrastructure.

DESNZ have appointed a supplier to improve threat detection and information sharing across the GB energy sector by establishing an automated threat sharing service that enables faster, more consistent and more secure exchange of machine-readable technical indicators.

tender.title: Ratton School Specialist Base - Quantity Surveyor Consultancy Services
tender.description:
East Sussex County Council (ESCC) requires the appointment of an independent Project Manager and Technical Advisor (PM/TA) to support the delivery of a school project utilising a Modern Methods of Construction (MMC) solution. The PM/TA will provide overall project management, governance, programme management, stakeholder engagement, risk and change management, together with independent technical assurance throughout the design, manufacture, construction, commissioning and defects phases of the project.

The requirement is needed to ensure ESCC acts as an informed client and receives objective, evidence-based advice throughout the project lifecycle. Given the specialist nature of MMC delivery and the need to maintain robust oversight of programme, quality, statutory compliance, design development and construction activities, ESCC requires an experienced consultant capable of providing both project
management leadership and independent technical assurance.

The key objectives of the procurement were to:

• Appoint a suitably qualified and experienced consultant with expertise in project management and technical assurance for MMC projects.
• Provide ESCC with independent oversight and challenge of design,
manufacturing and construction activities.
• Ensure compliance with statutory requirements, Building Regulations, fire safety, accessibility standards and SEND-specific requirements.
• Support effective project governance, stakeholder engagement, risk management and decision-making.
• Protect the Council's interests by providing quality assurance, programme monitoring and independent technical advice throughout project delivery.
• Deliver value for money whilst ensuring successful project outcomes and minimising project risk.

tender.title: RPA Vendor Support
tender.description:
The requirement is for Rural Payments Agency (RPA) vendor support which is hosted across two datacentres, one for Development, Test and Disaster Recovery and the other for Production. Rural Payments Service (RPS) comprises of business critical applications including the Rural Payments Portal - Siti Agri, the Customer Portal and database, the Land Management System (LMS) and the Data Warehouse (DWH).

It is expected that some components will be replaced over the coming years, however there are others that are likely to remain for some time. It is likely that the Customer Portal and Payments Portal will remain in operation for several years until transition plans are confirmed.  

This is a critical service requirement, without this contract Defra Group will not be able to guarantee service continuity in enabling the RPS to make payments to landowners. This strategy is to safeguard a specific service that Defra requires and to investigate other longer-term options to move to the cloud and become more cloud native.

This is a critical service requirement, without this contract Defra Group will not be able to guarantee service continuity in enabling the RPS to make payments to landowners. 

The initial call off period is for 3 years with the possibility of 1+1 extension options to ensure continuity of a critical requirement.

tender.title: HULL CITY COUNCIL- Door Access Control Improvements 2024  (Various Sites)
tender.description: The Client Kingston upon Hull City Council is in the process of standardising and improving its Building Access Control systems across its property assets. This contract is for the replacement of remaining "Tyco C-Cure" systems and Paxton Switch 2 systems (non-networked) across Eighteen sites, to Paxton Net 2 systems, thus allowing for a standard internal network-based system to coincide with the Councils security protocols. It is expected that much of the existing C-Cure system wiring (where applicable) can be re-used and adapted to operate on the Paxton System and where Maglocks/door locks are in place these can also be re-used along with their power supplies. The project works are across 18 Hull City Council buildings, all of which are occupied, operational and serve the public. The winning contractor will be expected to liaise closely with the Project Manager, client and building managers with regard s to the programming and delivery of the works to minimise disruption and impact on the services offered. Safeguarding will need to be considered at some sites due to the nature of the services offered and health and safety of the staff, public and visitors will be key across all sites.
